title: Seamless tiered routing recommendations and canary rollback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build a recommendation engine and safe rollout mechanism that applies per-customer and per-route batching and caching presets based on observed latency/cost/quality trade-offs. The feature should produce human-readable suggestions, an automated canary apply path, and a one-click rollback that is auditable and reversible. This reduces token unit cost while keeping end-to-end latency and quality within SLOs for different customer tiers.
background: We have several manual patterns: ad-hoc per-route config changes, brittle allowlist/denylists, and multi-customer mixed rollouts that caused regressions during prior cost-savings pushes. Recent telemetry shows 12% median token savings when safe batching and prefix caching are applied for certain route patterns, but customer regressions occurred in 2 regressions out of 18 canaries due to aggressive KV eviction and quantization mismatches. This initiative centralizes recommendations, enforces tier policies, and adds a canary+rollback workflow with deterministic metrics evaluation.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation engine generates per-route and per-customer config suggestions (batch_size, max_latency_target, prefix_cache_ttl) for >= 95% of traffic profiles seen in the sample window

Automated canary applies config to a subset (configurable by customer-tier and route) and measures cost, tail latency (p95/p99), and quality (prompt-level evals or smoke prompts) against a baseline for at least 24 hours
Rollback executes within 5 minutes of trigger and restores previous config for the canary cohort; audit log records causal metadata and who initiated the change
UI surfaces suggestions with rationale and expected impact (delta tokens / latency / cost) and provides an approval checkpoint for P1/P0 customers
Safety net prevents apply for routes/customers marked as 'deny-autotune' and escalates for customers in enterprise-tier unless explicitly opted-in
Integration tests exercising canary apply, metric comparisons, and rollback pass in CI with synthetic workload
implementation_plan: Data collection: add per-route sample windows (30m/4h/24h) for token distribution, seq-length histograms, and cache hit patterns
Recommendation engine: rule-based + lightweight ML ranker that maps profiles to preset configs; initial rules cover batching, prefix cache TTL, and conservative quantization profiles
Policy layer: enforce allowlist/denylist and tier-based overrides; admin API for marking routes/customers as "deny-autotune" or "allow-autotune"
Canary runner: orchestration service to apply config to percentage of traffic with metrics plumbing to compare baseline vs candidate
Rollback controller: maintain previous config snapshot, automated rollback triggers (regression thresholds) and manual rollback endpoint with audit entries
Console UX: suggestion cards, expected impact estimate, canary controls, and rollback button with confirmation and required approvals for enterprise customers
Tests & monitoring: synthetic prompts for quality smoke checks, dashboard panels for delta-cost, delta-p95, and regression alerts
testing_and_canary_plan: Stage env: end-to-end run with 5 synthetic tenants and route patterns mirroring common distributions
Canary config: support 1%, 5%, 10% traffic splits by route and by tenant; default start at 1%
Regression detection: delta-cost > -2% with delta-p95 > +10ms or quality drop > 2% triggers automatic rollback
Manual validation: solutions engineer reviews quality smoke prompts for first canary before scaling to 10%
CI: unit tests for policy enforcement, integration tests for canary apply/rollback, e2e for audit logging
rollout_steps: MVP rollout to internal tenants and 3 opt-in customers
Monitor for 72 hours, iterate on thresholds and suggestion ranking
Enable automated canary for P2/P3 customers by default; require approval for P0/P1
Gradually expand to 25% of customer base over 6 weeks with weekly reviews
Post-mortem and tuning cycle after first 100 canaries
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive batching increases tail latency for interactive flows -> Mitigation: conservative batch_size cap per latency-sensitive route and p99 monitoring

Risk: KV cache invalidation causes semantic regressions for streaming stateful sessions -> Mitigation: exclude routes flagged as stateful from prefix caching; add a "cache-compatibility" check during suggestion generation
Risk: Incorrect allowlist/denylist rules block beneficial cost savings -> Mitigation: create "dry-run" simulation mode and human approvals for high-impact customers
Risk: Audit/logging gaps make debugging painful after rollbacks -> Mitigation: require snapshot and operation metadata be stored for 90 days and surfaced in Console
notes_for_reviewers: Focus reviews on safety thresholds and the policy override surface. Security team should validate that the canary runner cannot escalate privileges or alter non-runtime config. PM to confirm opt-in rules for enterprise customers.
